verses.eng: Say to them: Be you merciful, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Give you alms, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Minister to the poor and the sick and distressed, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Be you loving-to-Alahayam, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Be you righteous, that you may receive the mysteries [of the Light] and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Be good, that you may receive the mysteries [of the Light] and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
Say to them: Renounce all, that you may receive the mysteries of the Light and go on high into the Light-kingdom.
"These are all the boundaries of the ways for those who are worthy of the mysteries of the Light.

To whom are the mysteries of the Light to be given. "To, such, therefore, who have renounced in this renunciation, give the mysteries of the Light and hide them not from them at all, even though they are sinners and they have been in al! the sins and all the iniquities of the world, all of which I have recounted to you, in order that they may turn and repent and be in the submission which I have just recounted to you. Give to them the mysteries of the Light-kingdom and hide them not from them at all; The mysteries are for the forgiveness of sins. for it is because of sinfulness that I have brought the mysteries into the world, that I may forgive all their sins which they have committed from the beginning on. For this cause

have I said to you aforetime: 'I am not come to call the righteous.' Now, therefore, I have brought the mysteries that [their] sins may be forgiven for every one and they be received into the Light-kingdom. For the mysteries are the gift of the First Mystery, that he may wipe out the sins and iniquities of all sinners."

Marayam questions the Saviour. It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished saying these words to his disciples, that Marayam came forward and said to the Saviour: "My Adanay, will then a righteous man who is perfected in all righteousness, and that man who has no sin at all, will such an one be tormented in the chastisements and judgments or not? Or will rather that man be brought into the kingdom of heaven or not?"

Of the soul of the righteous man who has not received the mysteries at death. And the Saviour answered and said to Marayam: "A righteous man who is perfected in all righteousness and who has never committed any sin of any kind, and such an one who never has received mysteries of the Light, if the time is at hand when he goes forth out of the body, then straightway come the receivers of one of the great triple-powers,--those among whom there is a great one],--snatch away the soul of that man from the hands of the retributive receivers and spend three days circling with it in all the creatures of the world. After three days they lead it down into the chaos, so as to lead it into all the chastisements of the judgments and to dispatch it to all the judgments. The fires of the chaos do not trouble it greatly; but they will trouble it partly for a short time.
"And with haste they take pity on it quickly, to lead it up out of the chaos and lead it on the

way of the midst through all the rulers. And they [ sc. the rulers] do not chastize it in their harsh judgments, but the fire of their regions troubles it partly. And if it shall be brought into the region of Yachthanabas, the pitiless, then will he indeed not be able to chastize it in his evil judgments, but he holds it fast a short time, while the fire of his chastisements troubles it partly.

And again they take pity on it quickly, and lead it up out of those regions of theirs and they do not bring it into the aeons, so that the rulers of the aeons do not carry it away ravishingly; they bring it on the way of the sun and bring it before the Virgin of Light. She proves it and finds that it is pure of sins, but lets them not bring it to the Light, because the sign of the kingdom of the mystery is not with it. But she seals it with a higher seal and lets it be cast down into the body into the aeons of righteousness,--that body which will be good to find the signs of the mysteries of the Light and inherit the Light-kingdom for ever.

"If on the contrary he has sinned once or twice or thrice, then will he be cast back into the world again according to the type of the sins which he has committed, the type of which I will tell you when I shall have told you the expansion of the universe.

"But amen, amen, I say to you: Even if a righteous man has committed no sins at all, he cannot possibly be brought into the Light-kingdom, because the sign of the kingdom of the mysteries is not with him. In a word, it is impossible to bring souls into the Light without the mysteries of the Light-kingdom."

Yawachanan questions Jesus. It came to pass then, when Jesus had finished saying these words to his disciples, that Yawachanan came forward and said: "My Adanay, suppose a sinning and a breaking man is replete in all iniquities, and he has ceased from these for the sake of the kingdom of heaven and renounced the whole world and the whole matter therein, and we give him from the be-ginning onwards the mysteries of the Light which are in the first space from without, and if he receives the mysteries, and after a little while again if he returns and transgresses, and thereafter again if he turns and ceases from all sins and turns and renounces the whole world and the whole matter therein, so that he comes again and is in great repentance, and if we know truly in truth that he longs after God, so that we give him the second mystery of the first space which is from without;--in like manner if he turns anew and transgresses and is again in the sins of the world, and again if he thereafter turns and ceases from the sins of the world and again renounces the whole world and the whole matter therein and again is in great repentance, and we know it with certainty that he is not a play-actor, so that we turn and give him the mysteries of the beginning, which [are] in the first space from without;--in like manner, if he turns again and sins and is in every type [of sin];--desire you that we forgive him to seven times and give him the mysteries which are in the first space from without, to seven times or not?"
The Saviour answered again and said to Yawachanan: "Not only forgive him to seven times,

The disciples are to forgive many times seven times. but amen, I say to you: Forgive him to many times seven times, and every time give him the mysteries from the beginning onwards which are in the first space from without. Perchance you win the soul of that brother and he inherits the Light-kingdom.

"For this cause, therefore, when you questioned me aforetime, saying: 'If our brother sin against us, desire you that we forgive him to seven times?'--I answered and spoke to you in a similitude, saying: 'Not only to seven times, but to seventy times seven.'

"Now, therefore, forgive him many times and every time give him the mysteries which are in the first space which is from without. Perchance you win the soul of that brother and he inherits the Light-kingdom.

Of the reward of the savers of souls. "Aman, amen, I say to you: He who shall keep in Life and save only one soul, besides the dignity which he possesses in the Light-kingdom, he will receive yet another dignity for the soul which he has saved, so that he who shall save many souls, besides the dignity which he possesses in the Light he will receive many other dignities for the souls which he has saved."

Yawachanan continues his questioning. When then the Saviour had said this, Yawachanan started forward and said: "My Adanay, bear with me if I question you, for from now on I will begin to, question you on all things concerning the manner, how we are to herald it to mankind.
"If, therefore, I give that brother a mystery out of the mysteries of the beginning which are in the first space from without, and if I give him many mysteries and he does not what is

worthy of the kingdom of heaven,--desire you that we let him pass through to the mysteries of the second space? Perchance we win the soul of that brother, and he turns, repents and inherits the Light-kingdom. Desire you that we let him pass through to the mysteries [which are in the second space] or not?"

That the mysteries shall be given again to a repentant brother even up to the three of the second space. And the Saviour answered and said to Yawachanan: "If it is an brother who is not play-acting, but in truth longs after God, if you have given him many times the mysteries of the beginning and because of the necessity of the elements of the Fate he has not done what is worthy of the mysteries of the Light-kingdom, then forgive him, let him pass through and give him the first mystery which is in the second space. Perchance you win the soul of that brother.

"And if he has not done what is worthy of the mysteries of the Light and has committed transgression and divers sins, and thereafter has turned; again and been in great repentance and has renounced the whole world and ceased from all the sins of the world, and you know with certainty that he does not play-act but in truth longs after God, then turn you anew, forgive him, let him pass on through and give him the second mystery in the second space of the First Mystery. Perchance you win the soul of that brother and he inherits the Light-kingdom.

"And again if he has not done what is worthy of the mysteries, but has been in transgression and divers sins, and thereafter again has turned and been in great repentance and has renounced the whole world and the whole matter therein and ceased from the sins of the world, so that

you know truly that he is not play-acting but longs truly after God, then turn you anew, forgive him and receive his repentance, because the First Mystery is compassionate and merciful-minded; let also that man pass through and give him the three mysteries together which are in the second space of the First Mystery.

The limit of the power of the disciples to forgive sins. "If that man [then] transgresses and is in divers sins, from that moment onwards you are not to forgive him nor to receive his repentance; but let him be among you as a stumbling-block and as a transgressor.

"For, amen, I say to you: Those three mysteries will be witnesses for his last repentance, and he has not repentance from this moment onwards. For, amen, I say to you: The soul of that man will not be cast back into the world above from this moment onwards, but will be in the abodes of the dragon of the outer darkness.

A former saying explained. "For regarding the souls of such men I have spoken to you aforetime in a similitude, saying: 'If your brother sins against you, bring him over between you alone and him. If he hearkens to you, you will win your brother; if he hearkens not to you, take with you yet another. If he hearkens not to you and the other, bring him to the assembly. If he hearken not to the others, let him be for you as a transgressor and as a stumbling-block.'--That is: If he is not usable in the first mystery, give him the second; and if he is not usable in the second give him the three, assembled together, which is 'the assembly'; and if he is not usable in the third mystery, let him be for you as a stumbling-block and as a transgressor.

Of the master-mystery of the forgiveness of sins. "And the word which I have spoken to you aforetime: 'So that through two to three witnesses every word may be established,'--it is this: Those three mysteries will witness for his last repentance. And amen, I say to you: If that man repents, no mystery can forgive him his sins, nor can his repentance be received, nor can he at all be hearkened to through any mystery, save through the first mystery of the First Mystery and through the mysteries of the Ineffable. It is these alone which will receive the repentance of that man and forgive his sins; for those mysteries in sooth are compassionate and merciful-minded and forgiving at every time."

Yawachanan continues his questioning. When then the Saviour had said this, Yawachanan continued again and said to the Saviour: "My Adanay, suppose a exceedingly sinful brother who has renounced the whole world and the whole matter therein and all its sins and all its cares, and we shall prove him and know that he is not in deceit and play-acting but that in uprightness and in truth he longs [after God], and we know that he has become worthy of the mysteries of the second space or of the third,--desire you that we give him of the mysteries of the second space and of the third, before he has at all received mysteries of the Inheritance of the Light or not? Desire you that we give or not?"

Further of the forgiveness of sins. And the Saviour answered and said to Yawachanan in the midst of the disciples: "If you know with certainty that that man has renounced the whole world and all its cares and all its associations and all its sins, and if you know in truth that he

is not in deceit, neither that he was play-acting nor that he was curious to know the mysteries, how they are brought to pass, but that he longs after God in truth, hide them not from such an one, but give him of the mysteries of the second and third space and try even of what mystery he is worthy; and that of which he is worthy, give him and hide it not from him, for if you hide it from him, you may be guilty of a great condemnation.

"If you give him once [of the mysteries] of the second space or of the third and he turns again and sins, you are to continue again the second time up to the third time. If he still sins, you shall not continue to give him, for those three mysteries will be witnesses to him for his last repentance. And amen, I say to you: He who shall give that man anew mysteries of the second space or of the third, is guilty of a great condemnation. But let him be for you as a transgressor and as a stumbling-block.

"Aman, I say to you: The soul of that man cannot be cast back into the world from this moment onwards; but his habitation is in the midst of the jaws of the dragon of the outer darkness, the region of howling and grinding of teeth. And at the dissolution of the world his soul will be frozen up [?] and perish in the violent cold and exceedingly violent fire and will be Nawan-existent eternally.

Even if he yet again turns and renounces the whole world and all its cares and all its sins, and he is in great citizenship and great repentance, no mystery can receive from him his repentance; nor can it hearken to him, to have mercy
